An exact premiere date hasn’t been announced, but the outlet is confident the release window is considerably later than the expected late 2026 launch, which showrunner Lauren Schmidt Hissrich previously indicated. Netflix hasn’t shared any official word or reasoning for the reported delay. The fifth season wrapped production in September last year, a month ahead of the fourth season’s airing. Filming on the fifth season partly took place in Cape Town, South Africa before heading back to the UK for the main leg of the shoot. The new run will mark the second turn of Liam Hemsworth as Geralt of Rivia, the Australian taking over the role after Henry Cavill exited the show following the end of the third season. Beállítom A rendőrség szeptember 15-én letartóztatott három újbudait, akiket azzal gyanúsítanak, hogy aranyfelvásárlással foglalkozó illegális üzletükkel több százmillió forintot csaltak ki többnyire idős áldozataiktól – írja a Police.hu . A 28, 50 és 53 éves gyanúsítottak nem egy módszerrel dolgozhattak, hanem mindig az adott helyzethez és személyhez alkalmazkodtak. Egy 71 éves sértett például több tízmilliónyi értékű arannyal ment be az üzletükbe, és a gyanú szerint felajánlották neki, hogy hazaviszik, hogy az otthonmaradt aranyat is megvehessék. Az üzletben ismeretlen folyadékot itattak vele, és a sértett ezután az utcán, sérülésekkel tért magához, az aranyékszerei nélkül. Egy másik idős sértettet az utcán szólítottak le, és azt mondták neki, hogy meg akarják venni az ingatlanát. A lakásba bejutva összeszedték az ott található értékeket és iratokat, és később a férfi elhunyt feleségének hagyatéki eljárására hivatkozva aláírattak vele valamit, amiről később kiderült, hogy életjáradéki szerződés volt, így az idős férfi 145 milliós ingatlanát átíratták egy hozzátartozójuk nevére. Olyanok is voltak, akik befektetési aranyat vittek be az üzletbe, amire a gyanúsítottak azt mondták, hogy rossz minőségűek, ezért csak a korábban megbeszélt összeg töredékét fizetik ki érte – úgy, hogy nem is adták vissza az aranyat. A rendőrség szerint az áldozatok ilyenkor már órák óta az üzletben voltak, és az állandó frusztráló nyomás és túlerő miatt sok idős ember inkább elfogadta az alacsonyabb összeget, csak hogy szabaduljon, ezzel tízmilliókat veszítve. Egy esetben az aranyékszereket azonnal elkezdték feldarabolni, úgy, hogy még az üzlet sem volt megkötve, így hulladékaranyként csak az ígért összeg egy kis részét adták az ékszerekért. A házkutatás során közel 200 millió forintnyi aranyat és egyéb értéktárgyat találtak a rendőrök. A család három tagját egyelőre bűnszövetségben, üzletszerűen elkövetett csalás miatt hallgatták ki. Ukraine says Russian drones kill 14, hit Kyiv and Odesa infrastructure Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 28/09/2026 - 8:30 GMT+2 Ukraine reports 14 dead and 57 injured after a massive Russian drone barrage hits Kyiv and Odesa on 27 September, damaging schools, hospitals and key infrastructure. … More Ukraine reported that a man was killed after a Russian drone struck a non‑residential building in Kyiv ’s Solomianskyi district early on 27 September , according to the State Emergency Service . Firefighters found the man’s body while extinguishing the blaze at the site. At another location in the same district, a drone hit a single‑storey vehicle service station, starting a fire that emergency crews prevented from spreading to a nearby food establishment. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The SES said both fires were brought under control at around 3am , and released images showing firefighters working as flames rose from the damaged buildings. The attack came during a prolonged night of Russian drone strikes across Ukraine: the Air Force said Moscow launched about 170 attack drones , including 76 jet‑powered Shahed‑type UAVs . In Kyiv itself, officials reported additional damage in the Solomianskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts, including to a school, warehouses and communications facilities, with several people injured, among them two 16‑year‑old girls . In the Odesa region , authorities said a separate mass strike killed one person and injured two others, damaging a residential building , a medical facility , a hotel , a shop and a grain storage site . Overall, Ukrainian officials said at least 14 people were killed and 57 injured across the country in the 26–27 September attacks, as Russian forces continued a series of strikes on cities and critical infrastructure . https://www.thespiritsbusiness.com/2026/.text: Menu News Stock Spirits reaches highest sustainability score to date 24 September 2026 By Miona Madsen Sierra Tequila owner Stock Spirits Group has been awarded the EcoVadis Gold medal for a third consecutive year. Stock Spirits Group’s EcoVadis score has risen by 58% since 2022 This year, the group achieved its highest-ever sustainability score of 87 out of 100. The result reflects a five-point increase, reportedly placing Stock Spirits Group in the top 1% of spirits producers evaluated by EcoVadis and in the top 5% of more than 175,000 companies assessed globally. Steven Libermann , CEO of Stock Spirits Group, said: “This is our best result yet, and we are proud to have once again improved our EcoVadis score and retained our Gold medal. “At a time when many companies are stepping back from their sustainability commitments, we are strengthening ours, building a robust ESG agenda and delivering on it step by step.” Stock Spirits Group enhanced its performance in three of EcoVadis’ four assessment areas over the year. Its Labour & Human Rights score improved by seven points to 88, its Ethics score rose by nine points to 82, and its Sustainable Procurement score increased by six points to 83. The Environment score remained stable at 91, which is classed as Outstanding. Additionally, the group achieved Leader status in the EcoVadis Carbon Rating, the highest assessment level. In just two years, Stock Spirits Group advanced from Intermediate in 2024 to Advanced in 2025, and now to Leader in 2026. EcoVadis’ assessment recognises the group for having a strong greenhouse gas management system, along with best-in-class decarbonisation commitments, actions, and reporting capabilities. Radosław Lewandowski, sustainability director at Stock Spirits Group, added: “This progress reflects the work happening across the group, from reducing our environmental impact and working more closely with suppliers to strengthening our approach to ethics and supporting our people. “There is more to do, and our focus now is on continuing that progress, including the validation of our science-based emissions reduction targets and delivery of our roadmap to reduce Scope 3 emissions by 2030.” Since 2022, Stock Spirits Group’s EcoVadis score has risen by 58%. This is said to be significantly higher than the broader spirits industry average increase of 11% across EcoVadis assessments. The EcoVadis result follows the release of Stock Spirits Group’s Sustainability Report 2025 and the submission of its emissions reduction targets for validation by the Science Based Targets initiative. Stock Spirits aspires to achieve an EcoVadis Platinum medal by 2027. Last month, the company announced two appointments : Paola Agasso as chief financial officer and Robert Sas as managing director in Poland. https://www.businessinsider.com/found-wa.text: Two years ago, when my family of four flew from Dallas to Scotland via London, our young children barely slept on the 10-hour economy flight, leading to meltdowns and frustration. So, when we planned our trip to Europe earlier this year, my husband and I wanted to do anything we could to avoid this travel chaos. Ideally, that meant booking upgraded seats to make our long flights more comfortable. Our main goal was business class, but we couldn't justify spending over $10,000 on upgrades, so we planned to use credit-card points. We had a lot to work with because we use primarily use just one Capital One card to earn points on everything we spend. Unfortunately, finding flights that worked with our schedule, points, and family wasn't so easy. For one, credit-card travel portals usually don't show every flight available with points. Airlines also limit the number of tickets available for points, making it difficult to find deals that work for a group. After spending hours opening dozens of tabs across different travel websites and scrolling through all sorts of deals, we decided to see if an online search tool might help. There are several different search engines and tools out there that help people find the best ways to optimize their credit-card points, whether they're booking hotels or flights. My husband did some research online, and we ended up trying PointsYeah to find upgraded flights that worked for us. On this searchable tool, we were able to enter details like how much we wanted to spend and with which carrier, the specific dates we wanted to travel, and our departure and arrival cities. From there, when flights that met our criteria appeared, we could receive an alert via email. PointsYeah's free version felt quite robust, especially for real-time searches, but we upgraded to a yearly plan for about $120 because it allowed us to set up to 32 point alerts, versus only four with the free version. We used the extra alerts to search by country rather than just by a specific airport, which gave us more flexibility and proved extremely useful. Departure city can be a major factor in international-flight prices, so we kept ours open to anywhere in the US. We were OK with booking separate tickets to travel from Denver to the official starting point of the international leg of our trip, provided the price was right. We also kept our arrival airport flexible between Krakow and Warsaw, and looked for specific ticket types (preferably business, but we were open to premium economy) for four people. Within a few days of setting up our alerts, we found our return flights. It was a bit strange booking the return first, but the deal was too good to pass up. It took us several more weeks to find an outbound flight we liked, and that meant sorting through alerts daily. Eventually, we found a points deal that we were happy with, and the alerts helped us act quickly. Once we decided to move forward with a flight, the process became a little more complex. After PointsYeah found me an option I liked, that process was in my hands. For this step, I had to visit each airline's website — in this case, KLM for a flight operated by Air France, and Air Canada for a flight operated by SWISS — set up an account, transfer our points from Capital One, and then purchase through the airline. I've found it can be tricky to convert credit-card points to miles on different airlines, so this part wasn't my favorite. Notably, some competitors, like Points.me, offer concierge services that will transfer points and book flights for you for an added fee (about $200 a person). The best flight deal we found from the United States to Poland had us flying from Chicago to Warsaw through Paris. To reach our international starting point, we bought separate tickets from our home airport in Denver to Chicago for $217.40 per person. From Chicago, we secured premium-economy seats on Air France for 75,500 points per adult and 56,625 points per child, plus $249.30 per person in fees. Though premium economy wasn't what we were hoping for, the extra legroom was well worth it. We even had enough room to place inflatable footrests in front of the kids after takeoff, letting them stretch out and sleep. On our return flight, we flew out of Zurich in business class on Swiss Air to Washington Dulles and connected to Denver, costing us 70,000 points per person and $165 in additional fees. We could lie completely flat, and we had plenty of legroom and access to a larger bathroom, which was very helpful with young kids. For our family of four, the outbound leg of our trip cost $1,866.80 and 264,250 points, and the inbound leg cost $660 and 280,000 points, for a total of $2,526.80 and 544,250 points. Had we purchased upgraded premium economy and business-class seats for cash on similar flights, it would have cost over $17,000 — an expense we definitely could not justify. Ultimately, we loved getting to skip the overwhelming, time-consuming process of sifting through page after page of points deals across different airlines. Being able to explore all our options in one spot and set alerts to only be notified of what works for us was really helpful. Although parts of the process were more complicated than we expected — we still had to transfer points and book our own tickets — PointsYeah helped us snag upgraded flights for our family that actually worked with our budget. The best tool for you will depend on your needs and preferences, but it's nice to know services like this exist, and we'll absolutely be using them again.
